scope: 25 exact historical keys outside other assignments; full old operators, endpoint meaning/stance and successor claims compared with completed source component review.

rows.review_disposition: The Year V result created the political crisis preceding Fructidor, but did not mechanically cause the coup. Retire the simple causes edge with C83/48B preserving electoral rejection, heterogeneous winners, executive division and subsequent military intervention.

016962 preserves Artois’s organizational leadership of émigrés. Keep later western authority and limits separately in 8EB; a Quiberon or Condé projection does not mean he commanded every émigré force.

56435 can internalize conservative section dominance after Prairial furnishing the organizational base for Vendémiaire. Preserve opposition to self-entrenchment and uncertainty about royalist numbers, not a unanimous Parisian restoration programme.

60DA/43E040 must retain the army’s search for British connection at Granville and failed timing/information. A broad seeks edge can retire if this precise linkage remains explicit; British support did not originate the uprising.

B888 must retain failure of armed options redirecting royalism toward elections. Retirement of an unresolved target is acceptable only with the strategic transition explicit, not disappearance of royalism.

7593 must retain successive waves and changing social/political composition, with 8A61 where appropriate. Quiberon and Condé are later episodes, not substitutes for all 1789–1791 motives or proof of one aristocratic programme.

0848 can internalize majority Catholic recognition alongside religious freedom, state payment/nomination/oaths and the property settlement. Preserve stronger Roman spiritual authority while distinguishing reduced institutional wealth and state dependence; this did not restore the old Church or an exclusive state faith.
4E189 can internalize social resentment contributing to radical revival on 324–325. Preserve visible fortunes and material hardship without implying every sufferer adopted Babeuf’s programme.

Preserve the failed-invasion and post-Valmy collapse sequence in DCF/7593. General foreign dependence and the Brunswick threat are related but not equivalent predicates; remove unrelated Louis XVIII projection and distinguish princely retreat from participation in the cannonade.

5193/F6ED must preserve successive inflationary collapse, failed mandates and post-paper deflation/coin scarcity. The chronology is mediated, so do not imply assignat abandonment alone immediately caused every deflationary effect.

733FB can internalize official favour for Theophilanthropy within post-Fructidor religious policy. Preserve La Révellière, church access and weak mass appeal; reject any suggestion of a successful universal substitute for Catholicism.

4F5D/304796 must retain the specific unrealized Condé–Lyonnais link, Austrian dependency and later Pichegru schemes. Retiring a vague link is acceptable with the named planning route explicit, not merely two labels.
CEC665 can internalize renewed war and Rastadt as marking collapse of Campo Formio. Preserve ultimatums, troop transit and sequence; the delegates’ murder was not the sole originating cause of war.
B888 can internalize factional divisions limiting Clichy’s coordination. Preserve its important parliamentary organization and tactical cooperation without calling it a disciplined restoration party.
DCF retains the manifesto’s immediate counterproductive effect. Retire the broad direct link to all armed royalist defeat by 1797, preserving that wider defeat’s multiple causes in 069F.

33CF must retain the princes’ 1791 letter as an articulation of restorationist claims. 1DB77 is the Royal Session, not this manifesto: retain only the programme’s explicit backward reference there, with the source’s 13/23 June discrepancy preserved, and remove any identity projection.

Year III’s constitutional stability aim is not identical to later electoral authoritarianism. Retire purpose_of as an unqualified endorsement; retain CB77’s design and F4D/29CD’s coups undermining confidence in that design.

032D can internalize betrayal/arrest leading to prosecution and wider subscriber-list repression. Preserve Vendôme’s distance, the special court and administrative purge, with timing on 326/330 distinguished.

3F2B must retain rejection of Jourdan’s emergency motion as a decisive limit on resurgence. It evidences political opposition to exceptional procedure, not normative proof that all anti-Jacobin repression was justified.
As for the inverse row 452, retain the 1791 manifesto’s restorationist articulation in 33CF. Do not merge it with the 1789 Royal Session merely because it invokes an earlier royal programme.

2FE1/A4EB/E37B can retain sister-republic expansion as a combination of liberation claims and coercive French power. Preserve heterogeneous local foundations, military initiative, extraction and European alarm rather than treating every republic as identical.

38C9 preserves Favras/Mirabeau as contrasting forms of royal rescue/advice on 299. Keep Mirabeau’s constitutional aims distinct from counter-revolutionary restoration and ambiguous links in the Favras affair.
CB77 can internalize stability against extremes as a constitutional purpose on 318–319. Later coups show failure to trust the design; they are not part of its original legal machinery.

Pillnitz encouraged princely claims and was invoked in their manifesto, despite conditional foreign intentions. Retire the generic used_by edge only with that specific political use in 04E/33CF and the difference between expectation and commitment explicit.

2E013 should preserve the 1796 Paris peace mission as a predecessor to Lille, with French delay during Irish expedition planning. Use 215 for the earlier mission and 217–218 for Lille; do not bind the entire later negotiation to 215 alone.
